items.title: Carol Bash interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2012
items.q: this woman, Rina Kosersky, my music supervisor, was a huge fan of Mary Lou Williams, although she ended up not being my music supervisor. She’s now working with a foundation. What I did was make a phone call to her and say “how much money should I put in the budget for music?”

ctx.x: And are you able to — at what point do you put that in your funding applications? How do you — you know what I mean — because you don’t necessarily know what music you’re going to use from the get-go.

Um hum. Well what I would do is initially, I mean I always had a music supervisor in mind, someone who has a really good history of working with other filmmakers who I admire. And actually, excuse me, this woman, Rina Kosersky, my music supervisor, was a huge fan of Mary Lou Williams, although she ended up not being my music supervisor. She’s now working with a foundation. What I did was make a phone call to her and say “how much money should I put in the budget for music?” So basically it might not be the ©…
most accurate figure but it’s based on her knowledge and her expertise and so that figure goes into the budget.
